endorsements.quote: Therefore, SRHR programs considering chatbot integration should prioritize domain-specific content adaptation, expert-informed quality assurance, and thoughtful integration within existing service delivery and referral systems.

Transparent communication about data practices, coupled with robust encryption and adherence to relevant legal standards, are foundational to maintaining confidentiality and autonomy in sensitive health domains ( 41 , 42 ).

unlisted_practices: Position chatbots as complementary components within integrated SRHR strategies rather than standalone solutions.
Conduct rigorous evaluation of SRHR chatbots using randomized controlled trials, standardized outcome measures, larger samples, and longer follow-up.
Ground SRHR chatbots in established behaviour-change or educational theories and articulated conceptual frameworks.
Adopt hybrid chatbot models combining generative dialogue with structured verified health databases and clear pathways to human support.
Provide clear referral mechanisms to qualified providers when risks are detected in chatbot interactions.
Monitor chatbots for harmful responses and maintain audit trails.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary discussing the evidence, limitations, and ethical/governance considerations of chatbots in sexual and reproductive health.
